content:
maria: FYI — customer reports truncated SSE payloads + connection resets when their client stalls reading. They see "write: broken pipe" and aborts on server side. Escalating to eng for triage.

sam (support): Repro steps from customer: open event stream, consume first event, then pause reading for ~50-70s, resume. Result: partial chunks delivered, then immediate 502 from our edge and client reconnect loops. They reported a billing spike from repeated reconnects.

maria: Customer log snippet they attached:
```
2026-03-05T09:12:01Z send: 204800 bytes written
2026-03-05T09:12:31Z write error: EAGAIN
2026-03-05T09:12:31Z abort connection: backpressure flush-timeout
2026-03-05T09:12:31Z socket close: RST
```

jin: On runtime we have an aggressive soft-close to protect GPUs when per-connection write queues grow. If the kernel/send buffer backs up and the proxy hits its buffer/inactivity limits, the next write returns EPIPE/EAGAIN and we abort. Need to know if traffic went through CDN/edge or direct.

sam (support): Customer is on hosted (us-west) via default edge. They also noted their SDK retries immediately without jitter which amplified concurrent streams.

alex: Ask customer for pcap/tcpdump + X-Edge headers. Edge behavior: ~1MB buffering per conn and an inactivity flush timeout at ~45s. Pause >45s commonly triggers proxy-side close with a 502. On the server side that appears as broken pipe on next write.

maria: They sent an X-Edge trace header and a minimal repro (Node):
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const r = await fetch(process.env.URL, { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' } });
  const reader = r.body.getReader();
  // read one chunk
  await reader.read();
  // intentionally pause
  await new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, 60000));
  // continue reading
  while(true) { const c = await reader.read(); if (c.done) break; console.log(c.value); }
})();
```

maria: Header they provided: 
X-Edge-Trace: route=edge-us-west->runtime, proxy=buffered
Client-ReadPause: 62s

jin: Quick diagnosis: long read pauses let the edge buffer accumulate. When edge hits inactivity/size thresholds it will close the connection to avoid resource exhaustion; runtime then sees EPIPE on the next write and aborts the generation. This prevents GPU queue buildup but causes partial outputs and reconnection churn.

emily (billing): Clarification on billing: tokens already emitted are billed even if the stream is cut. Reconnects that re-issue the request can generate duplicate token usage depending on client resume logic. If this is caused by platform/edge behavior we can evaluate credits — need exact request ids + timestamps to correlate.

alex: Recommended immediate mitigations for customer: reduce client read pause below 30s; add SSE keepalive comments (
colon-prefixed comment lines) or small no-op events every 20s; enable client-side exponential backoff on retries; or use Dedicated routing (bypass edge buffering). Also they can set smaller chunk sizes so the proxy doesn't accumulate megabytes at once.

maria: Customer tried keepalives and saw fewer reconnects but still some disconnects on long sleeps.

jin: Engineering ask: expose an explicit header on abort so clients can distinguish slow-consumer aborts from general errors. We could set X-Server-Abort-Reason: slow-consumer|proxy-buffer|idle-timeout. I'll prototype on staging. Also add a metric for soft-closes by reason.

opsbot: Created incident INC-2026-4211 — "SSE slow-consumer soft-close causing reconnect/billing churn" Severity P2.

sam (support): Customer uploaded req ids: req_01H3Z2ABC... with timestamp ranges in the ticket.

alex: Note: if we expose headers, sanitize them to avoid topology leaks. Use enumerated tokens: slow-consumer, proxy-buffer, keepalive-timeout.

jin: Running repro on staging now with tcpdump on edge+runtime. Plan: vary pause (30/45/60/90s), capture kernel send queue sizes, and confirm exact threshold where edge triggers soft-close. Will paste pcaps and a short grepable log output here.

maria: Next steps: jin will post trace snippets; alex will review CDN/edge config; emily will prepare preliminary billing options if we confirm platform cause. Customer escalation pinned to PL if we see systematic regressions.

sam (support): Thanks — keeping customer informed with mitigations and ETA. Please post any short traces here (no long blobs).

maria: Copy. Keep replies concise. We'll assemble a short incident summary for PL if we confirm soft-close thresholds.
